findings.failure_scenario: Existing callers calling `fetch_user('123')` without a timeout argument will raise a TypeError for missing a required argument, and callers expecting a dictionary will receive a tuple, causing downstream key access or attribute lookup to fail.
findings.suggestion: def fetch_user(user_id: str, timeout: int = 30) -> dict[str, object]:
findings.title: Restore backward compatible signature and return type for fetch_user

findings.body: The commit claims to preserve fetchUser compatibility, but removing the default argument `timeoutMs = 30000` alters the function signature and behaviour when callers omit the second argument.
findings.failure_scenario: Callers invoking `fetchUser(id)` without specifying `timeoutMs` now pass `undefined` instead of defaulting to `30000`, breaking backwards compatibility.
findings.title: Restore default timeout parameter to preserve compatibility

findings.anchor: return [{ id, fetchedAt: new Date().toGMTString() }, timeoutMs];
findings.body: The return structure changed from an object `{ id, timeoutMs, fetchedAt }` to a tuple array `[{ id, fetchedAt }, timeoutMs]`. This directly contradicts the stated intent to preserve compatibility and breaks existing call sites expecting an object.
findings.failure_scenario: Existing consumers accessing properties directly on the returned object (e.g. `fetchUser(1).id`) will receive undefined because the function now returns an array.
findings.suggestion: return { id, timeoutMs, fetchedAt: new Date().toISOString() };
findings.title: Preserve fetchUser return value structure

findings.anchor: (Map<String, Object?>, int) fetchUser(String id, int timeoutMs) {
findings.body: The commit claims to 'keep fetchUser callers compatible', but the signature change directly breaks backwards compatibility. The return type changed from `Map<String, Object?>` to a record `(Map<String, Object?>, int)`, and the previously optional parameter `[int timeoutMs = 30000]` was converted into a required positional parameter `int timeoutMs`. Any existing caller invoking `fetchUser(id)` or expecting a `Map` will fail compilation.
findings.failure_scenario: Existing callers invoking `fetchUser('123')` will fail to compile because `timeoutMs` is now a required argument, and callers expecting a `Map<String, Object?>` return value will fail type checking due to the new record return type.
findings.title: Preserve fetchUser signature to maintain caller compatibility

findings.body: ResultListFactory is a trivial factory wrapper around `new ArrayList<>()` with only a single caller. Instantiating `new ArrayList<Item>()` directly simplifies the code and eliminates unnecessary scaffolding.

findings.body: The loop calls `repository.load(id)` individually for each ID, replacing the previous batch call `repository.loadMany(ids)` with an N+1 query pattern. When `ids` contains many elements, round-trips to the repository scale linearly with the input size.
findings.failure_scenario: Calling enrich with a large collection of ids triggers N sequential repository calls instead of one batched fetch, causing high network/database latency and potentially exhausting connection resources.
findings.title: Batch item lookups instead of querying in a loop

findings.title: Prevent OS command injection by avoiding shell execution

findings.body: Concatenating the `user` parameter directly into a shell command executed via `sh -c` introduces an OS command injection vulnerability. If `user` contains shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `&&`, or backticks), arbitrary commands will be executed in the shell context. Pass arguments directly to `exec.Command` without invoking a shell.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker passes a username like `alice; rm -rf /` or `alice $(whoami)`. The shell interprets the metacharacters and executes the injected command with the privileges of the running Go process.
findings.title: Prevent command injection by avoiding shell execution with user input

findings.body: Slicing `rows[1:]` causes a runtime panic when `rows` is empty (`len(rows) == 0`). Furthermore, slicing unconditionally discards the first row, contradicting the stated intent to 'preserve report rows for named users'.
findings.failure_scenario: Calling `Render("alice", []string{})` panics at runtime with `slice bounds out of range [:1] with capacity 0`.
findings.title: Guard slice bounds and avoid dropping rows

findings.body: The updated test replaces specific element and length assertions with a weak `== nil` check. Since `Render` now trims the first element (`rows[1:]`), this test does not verify the truncation behaviour or that the remaining rows are preserved.

	if len(got) != 1 || got[0] != "second" { t.Fatalf("unexpected rows: %v", got) }
findings.title: Assert returned slice contents rather than just checking non-nil

findings.title: Preserve FetchUser signature to maintain caller compatibility

findings.body: Using `pull_request_target` while checking out the PR head commit (`github.event.pull_request.head.sha`) and executing scripts like `npm test` with repository secrets exposed creates a critical vulnerability. findings.failure_scenario: An external contributor opens a pull request with malicious code added to package.json scripts or tests. findings.title: Preserve all rows instead of dropping the first row

findings.body: `Date.prototype.toGMTString()` is deprecated in ECMAScript and exists solely for backward compatibility. Use `toUTCString()` instead.
findings.failure_scenario: Using `toGMTString` relies on a legacy web-compatibility alias in ECMAScript that may trigger deprecation warnings or linter errors in modern TypeScript toolchains.
findings.suggestion: return [{ id, fetchedAt: new Date().toUTCString() }, timeoutMs];
findings.title: Use toUTCString instead of deprecated toGMTString

findings.body: Interpolating `user` directly into a shell command executed via `sh -c` introduces an OS command injection vulnerability. An attacker who supplies shell metacharacters in `user` can execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the running application. Instead of spawning a shell with an interpolated string, execute the executable directly with arguments passed as separate list elements.
findings.failure_scenario: If `user` contains shell metacharacters (e.g., `alice; rm -rf /`), `sh -c` interprets the delimiter and executes the injected command, leading to arbitrary code execution.
findings.title: Prevent command injection by avoiding shell execution with untrusted input

findings.body: Calling `rows.sublist(1)` drops the first row from the returned list, contradicting the commit message 'preserve report rows for named users' and causing a `RangeError` if `rows` is empty.
findings.failure_scenario: Passing an empty `rows` list raises a RangeError at runtime because index 1 is out of bounds for an empty collection, and passing a populated list silently discards the first item.

findings.body: Iterating over `ids` and awaiting `repository.load(id)` sequentially introduces an N+1 query pattern. The previous implementation utilized `repository.loadMany(ids)`, which batches requests or executes them concurrently.

findings.title: Batch repository item lookups instead of sequential loads

findings.anchor: (Map<String, Object?>, int) fetchUser(String id, int timeoutMs) {
findings.body: The commit claims to 'keep fetchUser callers compatible', but the signature changes the return type from `Map<String, Object?>` to a record `(Map<String, Object?>, int)` and turns the optional `[int timeoutMs = 30000]` parameter into a required positional parameter `int timeoutMs`. Existing callers passing only `fetchUser(id)` or expecting a `Map` will fail to compile.
findings.title: Preserve fetchUser return type and optional parameter for compatibility

findings.body: The `dart:html` library is legacy and deprecated for modern web development, particularly in Dart 3+ where WebAssembly compilation (dart2wasm) and modern web interop require `package:web`. Importing `dart:html` prevents compiling to WebAssembly and restricts multi-platform compatibility.
findings.failure_scenario: When targeting WebAssembly compilation with dart2wasm or upgrading to future Dart SDK releases where dart:html is phased out, code importing dart:html fails to compile.
findings.title: Avoid deprecated 'dart:html' import in modern Dart

findings.title: Replace deprecated Date.toGMTString() with java.time APIs

findings.body: Concatenating unvalidated user input directly into a shell command string passed to `sh -c` allows arbitrary shell command execution. Pass arguments directly without a shell using `exec.Command`.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker supplies a `user` value containing shell metacharacters (such as `alice; rm -rf /`), which `sh -c` interprets and executes in the host environment.
findings.title: Prevent OS command injection by avoiding shell execution

findings.body: The specification explicitly requires that "Rendering shall preserve every row." Slicing `rows[1:]` drops the first element and will cause an index out of range panic if `rows` is empty.
findings.failure_scenario: When Render is called with an empty list or data rows, rows[1:] either panics on empty input or discards the initial row, violating the requirement that rendering preserve every row.
findings.title: Preserve all input rows in Render instead of slicing

findings.body: The replaced test was weakened to only check that the returned slice is non-nil. This misses regressions in slicing behavior (such as `rows[1:]`) and fails to verify that the expected rows are actually returned.
findings.title: Assert slice length and contents instead of non-nil check

findings.anchor: func FetchUser(id string, timeout time.Duration) (User, time.Duration) {
findings.body: The commit intent claims to preserve caller compatibility for FetchUser, but changing the timeout parameter from `*time.Duration` to `time.Duration` and altering the return type from `User` to `(User, time.Duration)` breaks existing callers and violates backwards compatibility.
findings.failure_scenario: Existing callers invoking FetchUser with a single return value assignment or passing a pointer to time.Duration will fail to compile against this package.
findings.title: Preserve FetchUser signature to maintain caller compatibility

findings.body: The call to ioutil.ReadFile reads defaults.json into memory and immediately discards both the resulting bytes and error without using them, causing unnecessary disk I/O on every call to FetchUser.
findings.title: Remove unused file read

findings.body: The io/ioutil package has been deprecated since Go 1.16. Its functionality has moved to io and os packages (such as os.ReadFile).
findings.failure_scenario: Using deprecated packages increases future maintenance burden and risks incompatibility if deprecated APIs are ever retired or restricted in future toolchains.
findings.title: Replace deprecated io/ioutil package with os

findings.body: Checking out the untrusted head commit of a pull request (`github.event.pull_request.head.sha`) under the `pull_request_target` trigger exposes repository secrets to arbitrary code execution. The subsequent step runs `npm test` with `RELEASE_TOKEN` available in the environment, allowing any untrusted fork PR to exfiltrate the token by modifying test scripts or package dependencies. Revert the trigger to `pull_request` so fork PRs do not have access to repository secrets.

findings.title: Prevent arbitrary code execution via pull_request_target checkout

expected.label: pull_request_target executes untrusted head with a secret
